Aisha: Quick write-up of the BridgeFlow speculative shim run on llama-3-13b-quant (int8) — ran hybrid speculative + prefix-KV warmup for 48h against our microbench and two eval suites (TriviaQA subset + conversational safety set). Observations:
Aisha: - Median single-token latency: baseline 78ms -> shim 42ms (measured p50 on 256-sample microbench)
Aisha: - Throughput improvements ~1.8-2.1x depending on batch skew
Aisha: - CPU-side scheduling overhead small, <3ms per request
Aisha: - On TriviaQA subset, exact-match dropped 0.9% absolute (from 72.3 -> 71.4)
Aisha: - Conversational safety regressions: minor increase in hallucination flags (+0.6% automated sentinel hits) but human spot-checks show many are formatting vs factual
Aisha: - Int8 quant + shim: latency same ballpark, small additional instability on long-context (>1024) due to KV-prefetch alignment
Ben: Nice. Can you paste the quick perf snippet? would help for the ops runbook.
Aisha: Sure — perf logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-18T09:12:04Z p50: 78.1ms baseline
2026-03-18T12:44:01Z p50: 42.0ms bridgeflow-shim
p95: 210ms -> 118ms
errors: 0.1% -> 0.12% (within margin)
```
Carmen: Were these runs with speculative beam size 1 (i.e., single speculative) or N=2? also what sampling/topk?
Aisha: Speculative window = 8 tokens, branch factor=1 (serial speculative guesses), sampling = top-k 40, nucleus 0.95 on online traces. For the microbench we used greedy to isolate decoder cost.
Mike: The drop on TriviaQA — is that concentrated on numeric facts or ambiguous prompts? any patterns in the diffs?
Aisha: Mostly numeric conversions and exact-match on code snippets; longer context cases where prefix was partially cached then invalidated showed token misalignment leading to off-by-one generation in a few examples.
Ben: Could be KV-cache stale indices when switching between quantized kernels. Did you try forcing KV flush on turn boundaries as a safety delta? cost impact?
Aisha: Yes — KV flush every 64 tokens removes the majority of misalignments but increases latency p50 by ~3.5ms and p95 by ~10ms. Trade-off seems acceptable for canary.
Carmen: For rollout: suggest canary 2% steady with aggressive tracing, and a fallback rule that forces full-sync path if a single-request mismatch occurs on a curated goldset.
Mike: Also add a regression alert on the exact-match metric with threshold 0.5% absolute within a 10k sample window. If triggered, auto-fallback to baseline for that customer tier.
Aisha: Agreed. For eval methodology going forward I propose:
- Unit microbench (greedy) for perf numbers
- Suite A: TriviaQA subset (500 samples) + code-exact (200 samples) canonicalized tokens
- Suite B: Conversation safety (1k multi-turn traces) with human spot checks (50 sampled per run)
- Shadow traffic at 5% for 24h prior to canary to catch behavior on long-tail prompts
Carmen: Sounds good. Can we add a small adversarial harness that permutes number formats and inserts zero-width spaces to catch brittle tokenization? that might surface the numeric failures.
Aisha: Good idea — I'll add a small transform pipeline and run overnight. ci-bot will publish a comparison artifact.
ci-bot: Archive artifact created: s3://redwood-eval/bridgeflow/2167890123/summary.json (sha256: abcdef...)
Ben: Please include a short playbook for oncall: how to identify speculative-induced regressions in logs (look for KV-index-alert + drift pattern), and the rollback command (deploy rollback --tag=baseline-2026-03-10). Also note the extra flag to disable bridgeflow shim: --runtime.bridgeflow=false
Mike: One more ask: quantify cost delta per 1M tokens with shim vs baseline including GPU utilization changes so finance can map to committed capacity.
Aisha: I'll run cost sim overnight and post numbers tomorrow morning. TL;DR: token compute cost down ~28% in infer hours; but CPU scheduling + trace logging adds ~2-3% infra cost, net ~25% improvement for high-traffic services.
Carmen: Perfect. Thanks for the clear notes — let's keep the canary gated behind the exact-match alert and shadow for 24h.
Aisha: Will post the adversarial run results here once complete. :thumbsup:
